Stacking context là một nhóm xếp chồng độc lập: mọi so sánh z-index chỉ diễn ra bên trong nó, và cả nhóm được xếp như một khối duy nhất so với bên ngoài.

- will-change với bất kỳ giá trị nào tạo layer

- flex/grid item có z-index khác auto

html
<div class="a">     <!-- opacity: .99 → tạo stacking context, z-index nội bộ: 1 -->
  <span style="z-index: 9999">A1</span>
</div>
<div class="b" style="position:relative; z-index:2">B</div>
<!-- B luôn nằm trên A1, vì so sánh diễn ra ở cấp .a vs .b -->

.component { isolation: isolate; }  /* nhốt z-index bên trong, không rò ra ngoài */

answer_html_en:
A stacking context is an independent stacking group: z-index comparisons happen only inside it, and the whole group is stacked as a single unit against the outside world.

What creates one:
- the root <html> element
- position other than static plus a z-index other than auto
- opacity below 1
- transform, filter, backdrop-filter, perspective, or a non-normal mix-blend-mode
- will-change with any layer-creating value
- isolation: isolate, contain: layout | paint | strict
- a flex/grid item with a z-index other than auto

html
<div class="a">     <!-- opacity: .99 → new stacking context, internal z-index: 1 -->
  <span style="z-index: 9999">A1</span>
</div>
<div class="b" style="position:relative; z-index:2">B</div>
<!-- B is always above A1, because the comparison happens between .a and .b -->

The two that surprise people, because nobody associates them with z-index: opacity: 0.99 (a common GPU nudge) and transform (a common animation tool).

css
.component { isolation: isolate; }  /* keeps z-index contained, no leakage */

Debugging takeaway: when z-index misbehaves, do not raise the number — walk up the DOM to the first ancestor that creates a stacking context; that is where the problem is.
